title: Daily Market Digest: October 2, 2026
subtitle: Markets Rally on Cooling Rate Hike Bets After Weak Jobs Report

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Climb as September Jobs Report Misses Estimates, Easing Fed Rate Hike Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equity markets posted solid gains today, with all major indices closing higher. The positive sentiment was primarily driven by a weaker-than-expected September jobs report, which significantly reduced the likelihood of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month. Growth and technology stocks led the rally, while bond yields initially tumbled before paring some losses.

items.headline: Tesla Surges on Strong Deliveries
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) shares jumped 4.65% after the electric vehicle maker reported third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 vehicles, surpassing Wall Street expectations.

items.headline: Nvidia Hits New All-Time High Amid AI Enthusiasm
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) climbed 2.4%, hitting a new all-time intraday high of $237.55. The semiconductor giant continues to benefit from robust spending on AI infrastructure and a recently announced $150 billion stock buyback program.

items.headline: Nike Tumbles on Weak Outlook
items.summary: Nike ($NKE) stock dropped 5.6% after the athletic apparel company reported a weak fiscal first-quarter revenue miss, issued a grim full-year outlook, and signaled deeper-than-expected sales declines and further layoffs.

items.headline: Seagate Plunges on Toshiba's HDD Production Plans
items.summary: Seagate Technology Holdings ($STX) sank 14.29% following a Nikkei Asia report indicating Toshiba's plans to double its hard disk drive (HDD) production capacity by fiscal 2027.

items.headline: September Jobs Report Disappoints, Cooling Fed Rate Hike Expectations
items.summary: The U.S. economy added a weaker-than-expected 29,000 nonfarm payrolls in September, significantly below the consensus forecast of 84,000 to 90,000 jobs. The unemployment rate rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings grew 3.0% year-over-year, the slowest pace in 2026. This data has led traders to significantly pare bets on an October Federal Reserve rate hike, with probabilities now below 21%.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary and Technology Lead Gains, Healthcare and Financials Lag
items.summary: Consumer Discretionary emerged as the top-performing sector today, largely boosted by Tesla's strong performance. Technology stocks also saw significant gains. Conversely, Healthcare and Financial Services sectors lagged, with financial stocks, in particular, underperforming the broader S&P 500 for the month.

items.headline: Micron Reports Robust Earnings, Fueled by AI Demand
items.summary: Micron ($MU) recently reported strong fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $33.42 per share, a substantial increase from the prior year, beating consensus estimates. Revenues surged 379.3% to $54.23 billion, primarily driven by strong pricing and AI-led memory and storage demand.

items.headline: Iran War and Geopolitical Tensions Remain a Macro Concern
items.summary: Ongoing geopolitical concerns, particularly the Iran war, continue to influence inflation and central bank policy worldwide. Rising government borrowing costs and tariffs also remain significant macro trends affecting market direction.
